issue_context.title: Error unloading entry 'DSMname' for button - on every restart
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I'm using the Synology integration. My server name is Plumbus. On every restart of Home Assistant, I see a log error as follows.
```
Logger: homeassistant.config_entries
Source: helpers/entity_component.py:172
First occurred: 8:16:59 AM (6 occurrences)
Last logged: 8:16:59 AM

Error unloading entry Plumbus for button
Error unloading entry Plumbus for camera
Error unloading entry Plumbus for sensor
Error unloading entry Plumbus for switch
Error unloading entry Plumbus for update
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 474, in async_unload
    result = await component.async_unload_entry(hass, self)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/binary_sensor/__init__.py", line 173, in async_unload_entry
    return await component.async_unload_entry(entry)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_component.py", line 172, in async_unload_entry
    raise ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")
ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!
```

I'm unsure why this is being generated. It doesn't look specific to the Synology integration, but I've not seen it on any other integrations.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.4.1, core-2022.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Synology

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/synology_dsm/

### Diagnostics information
[log.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8460094/log.txt)

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @hacf-fr, @quentame, @mib1185, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`synology_dsm`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1004) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hi

please enable debug logging, restart HA and provide the homeassistant.log after the error message appears again.
To do so add the following to your `configuration.yaml`:
```yaml
logger:
  default: info
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.synology_dsm: debug
    synology_dsm: debug
```

Note: it is better to drag the log into the comment (_which will add it as an attachment_) and not copy paste as it is hard to read logs in GitHub.

Further your network configuration looks strange, since you have assigned different IPs from same subnet on each LAN interface 🤔

I've had a good look through the debug log and I can't see the error message this time. Perhaps it is occasional rather than consistent. I will keep an eye on this - happy to close the issue for now.

Re the LAN interface setup, my DSM (DS918+) has two LAN ports so receives two IP addresses.

Hi @kellyatkinson,
I do have a comparable setup (DS720+) André 2 ethernet ports connected, so ha detects initially two DSMs, but I discard one and added the other one.
With almost every restart, I receive these messages. I have already deleted the integration, re-added etc., but not luck.

@mib1185 I will add debug logging and keep this issue updated.

Hi @mib1185,

please find my log with the errors below attached (size exceeds comment character limit).

[synology_dsm.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8462907/synology_dsm.log)
I'm having the same issue (response, just to indicate this isn't a unique case)

I have this exact same problem, and I guess this one is about the same: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/59153
Having the NAS attached twice to the same subnet with different IPs is a totally normal configuration for load balancing or redundancy. So assigning a different subnet or disabling one interface is not a nice solution. I also tried assigning a FQDN as it was mentioned in the other issue, but it is still discovered by SSDP.

Just for everyone's information: I have my Synology NAS & Integration running for +- 9 months, never had this issue, up until a few days ago (guessing since 2022.4.0).  Never juggled with different subnets of whatnot...
I have the DS214+, with two ethernet connections, cfr. what @ElStefan said.
This has popped up again. Let's leave the IP address issues aside, and try to figure this one out. What else can I help with here?

please enable debug logging, restart HA and provide the homeassistant.log after the error message occurs again
To do so add the following to your `configuration.yaml`:
```yaml
logger:
  default: info
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.synology_dsm: debug
    synology_dsm: debug
```
Further if possible please download and provide the diagnostics data for this integration.

Note: it is better to drag the log into the comment (_which will add it as an attachment_) and not copy paste as it is hard to read logs in GitHub.

---
BTW: consider to use a nic bonding, instead of two single nics in same subnet.

(Off topic but)
Thanks for the tip on the bonding - that's what I had always assumed was happening already with the two NICs. I've just enabled this now. For others' reference, [here is info on this from the Synology KB.](https://kb.synology.com/en-my/DSM/help/DSM/AdminCenter/connection_network_linkaggr?version=7).

Here's my log, and the diagnostics data for the Synology integration.
[home-assistant.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8498084/home-assistant.log)
[config_entry-synology_dsm-f934baef654ba433a9a7174447e319d9.json.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8498089/config_entry-synology_dsm-f934baef654ba433a9a7174447e319d9.json.txt)

You can find my home asssistant log above (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/69709#issuecomment-1094817786).
The diagnosis information are attached below.

[config_entry-synology_dsm-556c450f342613501b79ae978879ae08.json.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8499765/config_entry-synology_dsm-556c450f342613501b79ae978879ae08.json.txt)

> Here's my log, and the diagnostics data for the Synology integration. [home-assistant.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8498084/home-assistant.log) [config_entry-synology_dsm-f934baef654ba433a9a7174447e319d9.json.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8498089/config_entry-synology_dsm-f934baef654ba433a9a7174447e319d9.json.txt)

The issue occur, because you NAS is discovered twice and HA will update the config entry twice in short time

```
2022-04-16 07:53:22 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.synology_dsm.config_flow] Update host from '192.168.86.10' to '192.168.86.11' for NAS '1820PDN239902' via SSDP discovery
2022-04-16 07:53:27 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.synology_dsm.common] Unsubscribe entity: 1820PDN239902_SYNO.Core.SecurityScan.Status:status
[...]
2022-04-16 07:53:27 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.synology_dsm.common] Unsubscribe entity: 1820PDN239902_SYNO.Core.Upgrade:update
2022-04-16 07:53:27 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.synology_dsm.config_flow] Update host from '192.168.86.11' to '192.168.86.10' for NAS '1820PDN239902' via SSDP discovery
2022-04-16 07:53:28 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Error unloading entry Plumbus for binary_sensor

```

This will not happen, when link aggregation is used.
~~Nevertheless, I'll update the code, so that an successful loaded config entry will not be updated by SSDP discovery~~
Thanks. I can confirm I haven't seen this issue again since I did the NIC bonding. Cheers!

Hi all,
since the issue could be solved by implementing a correct nic bonding configuration, I would go to close this issue for now.

review_comments:
This is actually not correct. Just because it's loaded, doesn't mean it's functioning.
It only means it probably WAS functioning at some point but the IP may have changed later and the polling is now failing
One alternative would be to use something like https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/samsungtv/__init__.py#L120
